dedupe_keys.name: rba disclosures on retail payments service reliability

description: The Reserve Bank of Australia requires individual providers of payment services to households and businesses to publish statistics on the reliability of their services on their own websites, to make retail payment reliability transparent. Each disclosure gives a standard set of quarterly statistics on significant outages and availability for specified services: ATMs, branches, cardholder payments, card acceptance for businesses, access to accounts through online banking, fast account transfers and next-business-day account transfers. The RBA page lists the providers with links to their disclosures, and customers can find them by searching for payment service availability on a provider's site; the framework was announced in a media release of 15 November 2021 and is explained in a quarterly disclosures note. Access is free, but the data are spread across provider websites in their own layouts. No licence is stated. Coverage is Australia. Caveats: there is no single consolidated file, and definitions of significant outage follow the RBA standard but are applied by each provider. For simulation it gives per-service outage and availability statistics for retail payment channels, to calibrate disruption and recovery in financial service models. Related catalogue records include the RBA RITS system availability statistics and the BIS CPMI Red Book statistics.
